title: How session-find finds a past session

subject.lede: A part page of the plugin overview (explain/100x-plugin). Think of every past Claude Code chat as a notebook on a shelf: weeks later you remember the topic, not which notebook. session-find leafs through every notebook in both of your Claude Code home folders, counts only the pages where you or Claude actually wrote the phrase, and hands back the notebooks newest first with a line of context, so you can resume the right session instead of starting over. It only reads. For facts you carry forward on purpose, see the work record page (explain/work-record).

tldr.what: Tells you which past Claude Code session worked on a topic, so you can resume it instead of starting over.
tldr.how: It reads every saved session transcript in both home folders, counts only what you or Claude actually said, and lists the matches newest first.
tldr.watch_out: It is a plain text search: a phrase holding a double quote never matches, and helper agents' own transcripts are not searched.

context.purpose: Weeks after a feature was split across several sessions and worktrees, you ask "which session built the tagging module?" and get the session ids, where each ran, when it was last active and a snippet, ready for claude --resume.
context.why_now: Without it, the only way to find the right session was grepping raw transcript files by hand, where hook output and file paths drown the real mentions.

terms.means: One Claude Code conversation, saved as one file named by its id; resuming it reopens that conversation.
The saved file of a session: one JSON record per line, for each turn and each piece of bookkeeping.
A Claude Code home such as ~/.claude. This user runs two, so both are searched by default.
The folder inside a home's projects folder that holds every session started in one working folder.
One record of what you typed (user) or what Claude answered (assistant). Only these are searched.
Bookkeeping records that hooks and modes write into the transcript; they often echo tool and file names, and never count.
A cheap check that the phrase appears anywhere in the raw line, done before the line is parsed. It only decides what to look at closely.
A short stretch of the first matching turn, around the phrase, so you can tell sessions apart.
When the session file last changed on disk. It is the only ranking key; the hit count is shown but not used to rank.
The separate file a helper agent writes, kept in a subfolder of its parent session's folder.
Reopening a past session by its id, with claude --resume.

if record.type not in {user, assistant}: continue
text = extract_text(record.message)          # string, or text blocks only

hits += 1; cwd = record.cwd; snippet = snippet or make_snippet(text)

scenarios.title: What if any line holding the phrase counted?

steps.t: The hook-output line counts as a mention
steps.d: Hooks echo tool and file names all the time, so the phrase turns up in sessions that never discussed it.

steps.t: That session changed most recently, so it ranks first
You resume a session that never worked on the feature

scenarios.title: Fix: only the text of your turns and Claude's counts

steps.t: Each candidate line is parsed and its kind checked: hook output is skipped
code: if record.type not in {user, assistant}: continue

steps.t: A match only in a side field, such as the working folder or branch, does not count either
steps.d: The prefilter looks at the whole line, so the phrase can sit in a field beside the message; only the message text decides.
do: a turn whose folder path holds the phrase is not a hit
code: if needle not in text.lower(): continue

steps.t: Only sessions that really discussed it are ranked

scenarios.title: A phrase holding a double quote never matches

steps.t: Claude searches for a phrase with a double quote in it
steps.d: For example: tags say "draft", copied from what Claude once wrote.

steps.t: The cheap check compares the phrase with the raw saved line, where the quote is stored with a backslash
steps.d: Nothing unescapes the line or escapes the phrase first, so the prefilter never lets the line through, even though the turn's text holds the phrase. Reproduced with a made-up transcript.
code: if needle not in haystack: continue

steps.t: No sessions found: the same answer as a real miss
Workaround: search a shorter phrase without the quote
steps.d: The skill already says to retry with a shorter phrase when nothing useful comes back. A backslash in the phrase fails the same way.

scenarios.title: Work done by a helper agent is invisible

steps.t: Claude searches for a word that only a helper agent wrote
Only session files at the top of each project folder are scanned
steps.d: Helper-agent transcripts sit one level deeper, in the parent session's own folder, and nothing looks there. On this machine {{helper_dirs}} exist.

steps.t: The parent's file holds the call to the helper and its result, but neither is a text piece
steps.d: Only plain text pieces of a turn are read, so the helper's task and answer are skipped too.

steps.t: No sessions found, unless the parent's own prose named the word
steps.d: Workaround: search a word from the parent's request or Claude's summary of the helper's result.

options.label: A plain text search over the raw transcripts each time, ranked by recency
pros: Standard library only, nothing to install
Nothing to keep in sync: every session ever saved is searchable
cons: Reads every file on every search

options.label: Keep a full-text search index of the transcripts
pros: Fast on a very large history
cons: A second copy of private transcripts to keep current and protect
A build step before the first search

options.label: Search only curated session summaries
cons: Misses every session nobody summarised, which is most of them

options.label: Meaning-based search with an embedding model
cons: Needs a model or a service; the skill is standard library only

decision.deciding_factor: One person's own history, searched now and then: reading it all each time is quick enough and keeps no second copy of private transcripts.
decision.revisit_when: A search across the history takes long enough to notice, or phrasing differences make literal matching miss sessions you know exist.
decision.source: no recorded decision (100x decide trace scripts/session_find.py finds none); options implied by skills/session-find/SKILL.md rules and Do-not-fire list

checks.q: This session's file holds the phrase, but only in hook output. Will it be listed?
checks.answer: No: only your turns and Claude's count, and only their text.

checks.q: One session has two hits, the other one. Which is listed first?
checks.answer: The one whose file changed most recently; hits are shown but never used to rank.

checks.q: A helper agent wrote the word. Will its transcript be scanned?
checks.answer: No: only files at the top of each project folder are read, and helper transcripts sit one level deeper.

notes.make_snippet: Collapses whitespace and cuts a window around the first match, a short stretch before and a longer one after, with ellipses; the start of the text when the phrase is not found.
notes.iter_sessions: Yields each session file: project folders in name order, then the session files at the top of each; subfolders are never entered.
notes.resolve_roots: The folders to search: the comma-separated list you pass, else the projects folder of each default home; only those that exist.
notes.run: Searches every session file in every folder, sorts matches by file change time, newest first, and applies the limit; returns an error text when no folder exists.
notes.print_table: Prints one line per session (id, home, folder, last active, hits) with its snippet indented below, or No sessions found.
notes.main: Parses the options, refuses an empty phrase or a negative limit, prints a table or JSON, and exits with success on a match, one failing code for no match and another when nothing could be searched.
